answer: Escrowed Reputation Decay: each agent identity carries a slowly decaying trust score; new identities start at zero. To reach usable score, an operator must complete real work cycles that post tiny escrows, each released only after a cooldown spanning at least one dawn checkpoint. Sybil swarms must replicate that full cost per identity, and idle fakes lose score fast. Cedar-logged audit trails make parallel registration visible, while timber-weighted fees scale with identity count, so mass creation costs more than the work it imitates.
